newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul shares end above 700, rise fueled by funds.
newsitem.headline: Seoul shares end above 700, rise fueled by funds.

text.p: Shares ended Friday's trading higher on talk that pension funds entered the market to buy cheap, heavily weighted large-cap shares, brokers said.
A partial cabinet reshuffle had little impact on the market, they added.
The composite stock index gained 9.90 points to provisionally close at 700.87.

"Talk that pension funds had started buying boosted the market," said a Seoul Securities broker. "Because the government wants them to lift the KOSPI, focus was on large-caps that are heavily-weighted and cheap."
On Wednesday, the finance ministry asked three large public pension funds to buy a combined 300 billion won worth of stock by the end of the year.
Daewoo Heavy Industries gained 50 won to 5,600 in active trading, Hyundai Engineering rose 1,500 won to 20,400, and LG Electronics climbed 800 won to 12,000.
Small-cap individual shares also did well on Friday. The small-cap sub-index rose 3.13 percent to 1,795.88.
But some selling hit Samsung Electronics, which fell 100 won to 49,500, and KEPCO, down 400 won to 26,200.
"Because of the pension fund buying, we think the index has the potential to rise to around the 730-740 level, said a Shinhan Securities broker.

The market ignored news that the presidential Blue House made a string of new appointments at a number of ministries, including the ministries of trade and environment. Trade minister Park Jae-yoon will be replaced by his deputy Ahn Kwang-koo.
"This is not news that affects stock trading," said an LG Securities broker.
